find:
if (!VERIFIED_ANGLE_ARCHITECTURES.includes(arch)) return { kind: 'unverified', arch, actual };
  return actual === pinned
replace:
if (!VERIFIED_ANGLE_ARCHITECTURES.includes(arch) && actual !== pinned) return { kind: 'unverified', arch, actual };
  return actual === pinned
killedBy: angle probe does not treat an unverified architecture as a verified pass
why: The plausible-looking loosening: an unverified architecture whose hash HAPPENS to equal the x86-64 golden is reported as `verified-match`. It reads like a harmless optimisation -- the hash matched, so what is the harm -- and it quietly manufactures the cross-architecture bit-identity claim the owner's ruling on #484 refuses to make without repeated verified measurements and a maintenance story. One coincidental sample is not a verification. Invisible on x86-64, where the branch is never taken, which is why the killing case asserts the arm64-with-matching-hash pair explicitly rather than only the arm64-with-wrong-hash one.
